+def console_unknown_command_hint(self: Any, name: str) -> str:
+    """Return the Enter-again hint copy for an unrecognized `/name` draft.
+
+    Derived from the registry's own ``available_names()`` (Task 9) rather
+    than a hardcoded list, so a newly-registered command (e.g. `/skills`)
+    is reflected here automatically.
+    """
+    available = ", ".join(
+        f"/{name}" for name in self._console_command_registry.available_names()
+    )
+    return f"Unknown command /{name} — available: {available}. Press Enter again to send as text."
+
+
+def record_console_command_dispatch(
+    self: Any, parse: CommandParse, *, source: dict[str, Any]
+) -> None:
+    """Record an accepted command dispatch for usage ranking (TASK-18921).
+
+    Appends a minimal, content-free token — ``/<name>`` (plus the skill
+    name for ``/skills <name>`` invocations) — to the shared prompt
+    history, the existing local JSONL the ranking counts already mine.
+    Never records free-form command args. Fire-and-forget: history IO
+    is best-effort and must never delay or break a command, and the
+    command worker is never blocked on it. Ghost text is unaffected
+    (slash drafts never get ghost suggestions); Up-arrow recall gaining
+    past commands is the intended, standard-CLI reading of the store.
+    """
+    try:
+        history = self._ensure_console_prompt_history()
+        append = getattr(history, "append", None)
+        if not callable(append):
+            return
+        name = parse.name.lower()
+        if name == source["SKILLS_COMMAND_NAME"]:
+            first_arg = (parse.args or "").split()
+            text = (
+                f"{source['COMMAND_PREFIX']}{source['SKILLS_COMMAND_NAME']} {first_arg[0]}"
+                if first_arg
+                else f"{source['COMMAND_PREFIX']}{source['SKILLS_COMMAND_NAME']}"
+            )
+        else:
+            text = f"{source['COMMAND_PREFIX']}{name}"
+    except Exception:
+        return
+
+    async def _record() -> None:
+        try:
+            await history.append(text)
+        except Exception:
+            source["logger"].debug(
+                "Console command usage recording failed (best-effort)"
+            )
+
+    try:
+        source["asyncio"].get_running_loop().create_task(_record())
+    except RuntimeError:
+        # No running loop (a direct sync-context call): nothing to record.
+        pass
+
+
+def console_suggestion_usage_counts(
+    self: Any, *, source: dict[str, Any]
+) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """Return usage counts mined from the shared prompt history.
+
+    Best-effort display polish: every failure path returns an empty
+    mapping, which the ranking function treats as "no usage data" and
+    leaves the popup order identical to today's. Recomputed only when
+    the history store's ``revision`` moved (TASK-22218's cheap
+    invalidation key); ``entry_texts`` is an in-memory snapshot, so
+    this never blocks or triggers IO on the keystroke path.
+    """
+    try:
+        history = self._ensure_console_prompt_history()
+        revision = getattr(history, "revision", None)
+        entry_texts = getattr(history, "entry_texts", None)
+        if not isinstance(revision, int) or not callable(entry_texts):
+            return {}
+        cached = self._console_suggestion_usage_cache
+        if cached is not None and cached[0] == revision:
+            return cached[1]
+        counts = source["count_suggestion_usage"](entry_texts())
+    except Exception:
+        return {}
+    self._console_suggestion_usage_cache = (revision, counts)
+    return counts
+
+
+def rank_console_command_suggestions(
+    self: Any, suggestions: list[CommandSuggestion], *, source: dict[str, Any]
+) -> list[CommandSuggestion]:
+    """Rank popup suggestions by observed usage (TASK-18921).
+
+    Display-only: the filtered set is untouched when no row carries
+    usage (first run, or a fresh install), so matching and filtering
+    semantics are exactly today's.
+    """
+    if not suggestions:
+        return suggestions
+    counts = console_suggestion_usage_counts(self, source=source)
+    if not counts:
+        return suggestions
+    return source["rank_suggestions_by_usage"](suggestions, counts)

+"""Moved derivations retain screen state and live dependency ownership."""
+
+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from tldw_chatbook.Chat.console_command_suggestions import (
+    CommandSuggestion,
+    count_suggestion_usage,
+    rank_suggestions_by_usage,
+)
+from tldw_chatbook.UI.Console_Modules.command_handoff import (
+    console_unknown_command_hint,
+    rank_console_command_suggestions,
+    record_console_command_dispatch,
+)
+from tldw_chatbook.UI.Library_Modules.screen_helpers import (
+    source_study_context,
+    study_handoff_copy,
+)
+from tldw_chatbook.UI.Screens.study_scope_models import (
+    StudyScopeContext,
+    StudySourceItem,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.bootstrap_profile
+
+
+def test_command_ranking_reuses_only_the_current_history_revision():
+    entries = ["/model", "/model", "/help"]
+    history = SimpleNamespace(revision=1, entry_texts=lambda: tuple(entries))
+    screen = SimpleNamespace(
+        _ensure_console_prompt_history=lambda: history,
+        _console_suggestion_usage_cache=None,
+        _console_command_registry=SimpleNamespace(
+            available_names=lambda: ("help", "new")
+        ),
+    )
+    source = {
+        "count_suggestion_usage": count_suggestion_usage,
+        "rank_suggestions_by_usage": rank_suggestions_by_usage,
+    }
+    suggestions = [
+        CommandSuggestion(f"/{name} ", f"/{name}") for name in ("help", "model", "new")
+    ]
+    assert [
+        row.label
+        for row in rank_console_command_suggestions(screen, suggestions, source=source)
+    ] == ["/model", "/help", "/new"]
+    entries[:] = ["/help", "/help", "/help"]
+    assert [
+        row.label
+        for row in rank_console_command_suggestions(screen, suggestions, source=source)
+    ] == ["/model", "/help", "/new"]
+    history.revision += 1
+    assert [
+        row.label
+        for row in rank_console_command_suggestions(screen, suggestions, source=source)
+    ] == ["/help", "/model", "/new"]
+    screen._console_command_registry.available_names = lambda: ("fresh",)
+    assert (
+        console_unknown_command_hint(screen, "missing")
+        == "Unknown command /missing — available: /fresh. Press Enter again to send as text."
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_command_recording_retains_minimal_token_and_live_post_await_logger():
+    started, release = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()
+    entries, messages = [], []
+
+    async def append(text):
+        entries.append(text)
+        started.set()
+        await release.wait()
+        raise RuntimeError("PRIVATE COMMAND ARGS")
+
+    source = {
+        "asyncio": asyncio,
+        "COMMAND_PREFIX": "/",
+        "SKILLS_COMMAND_NAME": "skills",
+        "logger": SimpleNamespace(debug=lambda message: pytest.fail("stale logger")),
+    }
+    screen = SimpleNamespace(
+        _ensure_console_prompt_history=lambda: SimpleNamespace(append=append)
+    )
+    before = asyncio.all_tasks()
+    record_console_command_dispatch(
+        screen,
+        SimpleNamespace(name="SKILLS", args="name PRIVATE COMMAND ARGS"),
+        source=source,
+    )
+    (task,) = asyncio.all_tasks() - before
+    await started.wait()
+    source["logger"] = SimpleNamespace(debug=messages.append)
+    release.set()
+    await task
+    assert entries == ["/skills name"]
+    assert messages == ["Console command usage recording failed (best-effort)"]
+
+
+def test_library_study_derivations_keep_scope_and_current_source_copy():
+    has_sources, mode = [True], ["local"]
+    screen = SimpleNamespace(
+        _has_local_sources=lambda: has_sources[0],
+        _runtime_active_source=lambda: mode[0],
+        _local_source_records={
+            "notes": ({"id": "n1", "title": "Note"}, {"title": "missing"}),
+            "media": ({"id": "m1", "title": "Media"},),
+        },
+        _source_record_id=lambda row: row.get("id"),
+        _source_title=lambda kind, row: row["title"],
+        _source_sample_titles=lambda kind: {
+            "notes": ("Note",),
+            "media": ("Media",),
+            "conversations": ("Chat",),
+        }[kind],
+        _source_snapshot_body=lambda: "summary",
+    )
+    source = {
+        "StudyScopeContext": StudyScopeContext,
+        "StudySourceItem": StudySourceItem,
+        "MATERIAL_SOURCE_LIBRARY": "library",
+        "MATERIAL_TITLE_LIBRARY_SOURCES": "Local Library Sources",
+        "LIBRARY_STUDY_HANDOFF_MODES": {
+            "study": {
+                "header": "Study",
+                "action_label": "Study",
+                "button_label": "Continue",
+                "purpose": "Learn",
+            }
+        },
+        "_library_carries_forward_line": lambda titles: ", ".join(titles),
+        "LIBRARY_STUDY_HANDOFF_OWNERSHIP_COPY": "owner",
+        "LIBRARY_STUDY_HANDOFF_READY_COPY": "server ready",
+        "LIBRARY_STUDY_HANDOFF_LOCAL_MODE_COPY": "local manual",
+    }
+    context = source_study_context(screen, source=source)
+    assert context.material_titles == ("Note", "Media", "Chat")
+    assert context.material_summary == "summary"
+    assert context.source_items == (
+        StudySourceItem("note", "n1", "Note"),
+        StudySourceItem("media", "m1", "Media"),
+    )
+    assert (
+        study_handoff_copy(screen, "unknown", source=source)["recovery"]
+        == "local manual"
+    )
+    mode[0] = "server"
+    source["LIBRARY_STUDY_HANDOFF_READY_COPY"] = "current server ready"
+    assert (
+        study_handoff_copy(screen, "study", source=source)["recovery"]
+        == "current server ready"
+    )
+    has_sources[0] = False
+    assert source_study_context(screen, source=source) is None
+    copy = study_handoff_copy(screen, "study", source=source)
+    assert copy["context"] == ""
+    assert (
+        copy["recovery"]
+        == "Import sources or create notes first, or open Study globally without Library context."
+    )
